threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the tube' instead of 'TfL'—everyone here knows it's just part of the transport family.
Caught a night bus home and saw a chap in a full tuxedo arguing with a traffic cone, like it was his long-lost friend. London, eh?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I spotted a kid selling homemade lemonade next to a pile of abandoned bicycles, I knew this place had its own pulse.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You'd think buskers in the U-Bahn are all about music, but there's a guy in Kreuzberg juggling flaming torches while balancing on a unicycle. A whole performance!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know they’re from here when they get off BART at 16th and don’t flinch at the smell of street tacos mixed with the faint whiff of recent street cleaning.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a guy playing the accordion on the 6 tonight. The bus was packed, but his tune made everyone smile—even the guy in a suit who usually stares at his phone.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia’s plazas are just for pictures, but locals use them for proper conversations over coffee, day or night.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they still look up at the buildings; locals have perfected the art of walking while staring at their phones.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think it’s normal to wait for the bus in the rain without an umbrella. Everyone else has perfected the art of dodging puddles.
Caught a glimpse of a fox lounging on the roof of a bus stop on Coldharbour Lane last night—never seen one so relaxed in the city.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw the kebab shop owner arguing with the BVG driver over the latest strike—only here do you get street politics mixed with dinner plans.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You ever notice how in Kreuzberg, it’s common to see a full-on BBQ party in the middle of a street? Feels like every block could be a festival.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know they’re local if they can name at least three taco trucks along Mission Street and know which one has the best salsa.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus with a magician performing card tricks for passengers. The usual delays didn’t matter; everyone was captivated, laughing all the way.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: They think paella is a local dish. Here, it’s all about the escalivada and the pintxos at the corner bars. Totally different vibe.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newcomer by how they still hold their map upside down at the corner of Aribau and Casanova, looking lost among the locals.
